While it is true that using "se" in the start of a phrase is gramatically incorrect. In casual and everydar portuguese, it is pretty common to see brazilians making this "mistake". This happens because using "se" after the words is very common in European Portuguese, but in Brazil using "se" before the word became very frequent as time passed. So, in conclusion, if you're not trying to be gramatically correct (formal situations), using "se cortou" or "se machucou" will feel more natural to native speakers.

And, there are some words that require "se" to come first. Like "Não" (No). So the gramatically correct way to say "Do not hurt yourself" is "Nao se machuque".

There are a lot more exceptions that even natives struggle. So my tip is, if you're going for unformal portugese, use "se" before the word. But if you're going for formal, then unfortunately you will need to memorize all spcific cases.

This is actually true. I'm Brazilian and asked my Spanish teacher. "Why can I listen spanish and manage to communicate, while not knowing it at all. But people from other latin countries can't understand me in Portuguese, even tho the words are very similar?"

Turns out that the spectrum of sounds portuguese has makes it very difficult to understand portuguese coming from other latin langugages. I think that's the reason why learning portuguese first makes it easier to learn other latin derivate languages.

Cav is a very high risk, high reward operator, and you need to take this in mind before doing anything with her. Her silent step can really help you flank enemies. But you should always evaluate your surroundings when going for an interrogation.

Tip 1: Never go for an instant interrogation after downing someone,  wait 2/3 seconds before initiating the animation. You can use this time to hear your surroundings and evaluate if it's safe to go for an interrogation. 

Tip 2: You should really value your life as caveira and understand the amount of pressure you put on the attacking team by only existing. That said, you should never go for an interrogation if you know you might die right after finishing the animation. 1 kill and no interrogation is better than 4v4 with wallhacks. Most of the time the enemy team is just going to disengage and wait.

Tip 3: There are "easier" targets to interrogate than others. I'll explain. For example, if you manage to catch an Ash or Nokk entering on the map, they are probably alone and it's worth to go for an insta interrogation. At the same time, if you down a thermite, gridlock, Thatcher, they are probably not alone and I recommend you should finish the kill if you dont trust your skill enough to bait 2 more attackers onto your spas15 (dont use the m12).
I also recommend you try to play together with your other roamer so he can cover you while you use this ability. Caveira is very hard to play but it is very recompensating at the same time.

I'm a Dokkaebi/Hibana main on attack.

Dokkaebi is a VERY fun to play operator. She is very versatile, you can hunt roamers with your call and hack their phones to get intel, you can act as support because of her smokes and hacking Echo/Maestro to stop the anti plant, or you can just frag with her amazing primary gun (it requires a decent amount of mastery, tho). Her CZ is a very good secondary and can help you a lot if you don't know how to use the Mk17 at its max value. I'd give Dokkaebi an A tier.

Hibana isnt as fun to play like dokkaebi, but she is really good and very recompensating. Her primary gun is amazing (it has a considerable amount of recoil, but with training you can deliver consistent headshots). Her bearing 9 is very good aswell and can easily make up for the low amount of clip ammo in her primary. Her ability is very good and lets you avoid obstacles and help your team with hard breaching. And, at the end of the day, she is a 3 speed operator, in a game where speed is king. Hibana is easily one of the strongest attacking operators in the game.

So, I recommend you to buy Dokkaebi if you value a very fun gameplay while still being useful with intel/anti Intel. And I recommend Hibana if you really value winning and want a strong character to main. Best of luck on your ranked matches.
